projects.description:
The objective of the project is to address priority needs identified in coordination with partners and building on previous support from PRM for the refugee response in Jordan, IOM’s planned interventions for 2021-2022 are grouped under the following three outcomes: 
- Outcome 1: Vulnerable refugees outside camps are better able to meet their basic needs.

- Outcome 3: Refugees in Jordan have access to safe and dignified transportation for family reunification, documentation needs, and exceptional support for spontaneous returns to Syria.

projects.name: 1.1.2.50 -  Enhancing the Capacity of Jordan’s Border Authorities to Respond to COVID-19 and Mitigate its Socioeconomic Impact
projects.description: In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and its repercussions, this intervention aims to enhance the capacity of Jordan’s BA and the MoH to limit the spread of COVID-19 and the scope of the public health crisis, while also preventing the interruption of supply chains that border closures would cause, thereby mitigating the pandemic’s socioeconomic impact on Jordan.  This will be achieved by supporting BA with appropriate infrastructure and equipment, including Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), while also training staff present at Points of Entry (PoE) to screen, detect and safely handle, isolate, and refer suspected cases of COVID-19 and other communicable diseases, in line with IOM’s Health Border and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework.
projects.outcome: Output 1.1.2 - Improved Service Delivery for Human Capital Development and Poverty Reduction: Public Services in Health, Education, Social Protection, and Food and Nutrition Security have improved quality and are more accessible to vulnerable groups

projects.name: 1.1.2.48 - Strengthening Border Management and Security Practices at Points of Entry in Aqaba Governorate
projects.description:
IOM will support the Government of Jordan in their efforts to strengthen border management and security practices at Points of Entry (PoE) in Aqaba Governorate, and for Border Authorities to adhere to international standards and best practices for combatting transitional organized crime and terrorism at PoE while ensuring the continuity of cross-border traffic. The proposed interventions targets some of the country’s key PoE, focusing on the Seaport, the main land Border Crossing Point (BCP) and the international airport in Aqaba Governorate, the former being the principal PoE for commercial goods and travelers, and also situated alongside a regional drug-trade route, having seen regular seizures of trafficked drugs and other illicit goods in recent years.
Concretely, IOM will enhance the capacity of the Jordanian Border Authorities, namely the General Intelligence Department (GID), Borders and Residence Department (BRD), Jordan Customs and Anti-Narcotics Department (AND) by providing or upgrading technical equipment for enhanced border security and inspection, such as document verification devices, UV lights, magnifiers, etc. and based on identified needs, infrastructure for interview rooms, etc. IOM will also be supporting the development of protocols and operating procedures, based on identified needs and gaps, and by training frontline officers on key security elements of border management, such as identity documentation, risk analysis, and modus operandi of organized transnational crimes and terrorist groups in the region. The interventions will draw from IOM’s expertise in Integrated Border Management and Identity Management and Biometrics, while closely coordinating with other International Organizations, such as UNODC and ICMPD, to ensure that targeted interventions do not overlap with the ongoing activities of these actors but reinforce and is coherent with ongoing efforts to support the Government of Jordan in moving towards an Integrated Border Management system.
